'''Birmingham City Football Club''' is a professional [[association football|football]] club based in [[Bordesley, Birmingham|Bordesley]], [[Birmingham]], England. Formed in 1875 as Small Heath Alliance, it was renamed Small Heath in 1888, Birmingham in 1905, and Birmingham City in 1943.<ref name="clubname">{{harvp|Matthews|2000|p=55|ps=. "City was added to Birmingham (to make Birmingham City Football Club) in the summer of 1943 (and not 1945 as previously thought). The official Blues home programmes for the 1943–44 season clearly show Birmingham City Football Club on the front cover."}}</ref> The club competes in the [[EFL Championship|Championship]], the second tier of [[English football league system|English football]].

As Small Heath, they played in the [[Football Alliance]] before becoming founder members and first champions of the [[Football League Second Division]]. The most successful period in their history was in the 1950s and early 1960s. They achieved their highest finishing position of sixth in the [[Football League First Division|First Division]] in the [[1955–56 Football League|1955–56 season]] and reached the [[1956 FA Cup final]]. Birmingham played in two [[Inter-Cities Fairs Cup]] finals, in [[1960 Inter-Cities Fairs Cup Final|1960]], as the first English club side to reach a major European final, and again the [[1961 Inter-Cities Fairs Cup final|following year]]. They won the [[EFL Cup|League Cup]] in [[1963 Football League Cup final|1963]] and again in [[2011 Football League Cup final|2011]]. Birmingham have played in the top tier of English football for around half of their history:<ref name="footballsite">{{cite web |url=http://www.footballsite.co.uk/Statistics/ClubbyClub/ClubHistories/Birmingham.htm |title=Birmingham City |access-date=5 February 2017 |publisher=Football Facts and Figures |archive-date=7 January 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080107023446/http://www.footballsite.co.uk/Statistics/ClubbyClub/ClubHistories/Birmingham.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> the longest period spent outside the top division, between 1986 and 2002, included two brief spells in the third tier of English football, during which time they won the [[EFL Trophy|Football League Trophy]] twice.

[[St Andrew's (stadium)|St Andrew's]], currently known as St. Andrew's @ Knighthead Park since 2024 for sponsorship reasons, has been their home ground since 1906. They have a long-standing and fierce rivalry with [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]], their nearest neighbours, with whom they play the [[Second City derby]]. The club's nickname is Blues, after the colour of their [[kit (association football)|kit]], and the fans are known as Bluenoses.

As with most clubs, Birmingham City also operates its own charitable foundation that works across the local community, with a focus on breaking down barriers to participation through competitions like the [[Trevor Francis]] Schools Cup for secondary school children, and the [[Vertu Motors|Vertu]] Primary Schools Cup."}}
